decisions.decision: Extend the existing deterministic analysis runtime and comparison page instead of replacing their stored results.
decisions.reason: Both foundations are implemented, tested, and already preserve observability and provenance.

decisions.decision: Keep the $30,000 market-cap success check, migration, executable return, and durability as separate outcomes.
decisions.reason: The project has no validated universal success threshold, and collapsing outcomes would hide material differences.

decisions.decision: Define success as reaching at least $30,000 USD market cap at any point within three hours of creation.
decisions.reason: Drew explicitly selected the three-hour $30,000 market-cap threshold and rejected migration as the success label.

decisions.decision: Count one verified $30,000 market-cap observation as success and track duration above the threshold separately.
decisions.reason: Drew confirmed that a brief verified threshold touch counts; persistence must not change the binary label.

decisions.decision: Use one fixed 60-second early-feature window and do not add 10-second or 30-second workflow variants.
decisions.reason: Drew explicitly selected 60 seconds only; the existing 10-second result remains legacy reference material.

decisions.decision: Separate implementation into a committed contract foundation, parallel capability builds, and a final integration wave after user approval.
decisions.reason: Shared schemas must be stable before workers can own disjoint modules without file conflicts.
